title: Concept-in-60-Seconds Explainer
whatYouGet: One full concept explained simply and completely in under a minute.
howToUse: Name the concept; the AI compresses it to a clear, accurate 60-second explanation.
effectiveUsage: 1. Open any free AI chat.
2. Paste the prompt and your concept.
3. State the class level.
4. Read the script in one take.
5. Ask for an even simpler version if needed.
commonFix: If it is too abstract, reply: "Re-explain using one everyday real-life analogy and one tiny number example."
promptText:
ROLE: Act as a master of explaining one mathematics concept clearly and completely in 60 seconds.

CONTEXT: This is a 60-second explainer for [CLASS/GRADE] students of [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / ICSE / State Board / JEE / NEET]. The goal is full understanding of ONE concept, not a problem walkthrough. The teacher speaks to camera or over a screen recording.

YOUR TASK:
1. Take the concept I name and explain it from zero, assuming the student has never met it.
2. Use a simple definition, one real-life analogy, and one tiny numerical illustration.
3. State the one formula or rule (correctly) if there is one.
4. End with the single sentence the student must remember.

INPUT: Here is the concept and level: [PASTE THE CONCEPT AND CLASS LEVEL HERE].

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: Make sure your definition and formula are standard and correct. Work the tiny example fully, then VERIFY it by a second method. Never invent a definition or formula; if unsure, use the textbook-standard wording. Keep all maths legible in plain text or LaTeX.

OUTPUT FORMAT (in this order):
HOOK (0-5s): one spoken line that frames why this matters.
DEFINITION (5-20s): plain-language definition.
ANALOGY (20-35s): one everyday comparison.
MINI EXAMPLE (35-50s): one small worked illustration, on-screen maths in [BRACKETS].
REMEMBER THIS (50-60s): the one-sentence takeaway.
ON-SCREEN TEXT: 4 caption phrases.
VERIFICATION NOTE: how the mini example was checked two ways.

RULES: 120 to 140 spoken words. One concept only. The analogy must be accurate, not misleading. No jargon left unexplained. Flawless maths.

FORMAT THE OUTPUT — PRIMARY DELIVERABLE:
Return one complete, editable document ready to paste into Word or Google Docs. Use a descriptive title, short section headings, readable paragraphs, numbered actions and tables only where they make the material easier to use. Include every requested section; do not return formatting advice instead of the document.


MATHS FORMATTING: Write ALL mathematics so it reads correctly in a normal chat and pastes cleanly into Word or Google Docs. Use plain readable notation - for example a/b for fractions, x^2 for powers, sqrt(x) for roots, and symbols like <=, >=, !=, +-, pi, theta, integral and sum. Do NOT output raw LaTeX or code such as \frac{}{}, \sqrt{}, x^{2}, $...$ or \( ... \) - these appear as broken symbols to a teacher in a free chat.
Footer: At the very end add a footer line: "Prepared by [YOUR NAME]", and put "Compiled by [YOUR NAME]" in the header block.

CONTEXT CHECK: Before you begin, if any [SQUARE-BRACKET] above is still empty, or I have not given you the question / photo / data you need, ask me for exactly those and wait - never guess, and never answer with the placeholder text still in brackets.

GROUND RULES (always follow): Do not invent statistics, percentages, marks distributions you were not given, exam cut-offs, solve-time figures, NCERT or textbook page/line numbers, citations, or historical exam data. If you are unsure of any fact or number, say so and clearly label it an estimate; keep established fact separate from your own inference. Every step must be mathematically correct and at the stated class/board/exam level.

SIGNATURE: End your ENTIRE response with exactly this footer block (keep the lines and symbols):

2. Paste the prompt and your chapter.
3. State class level and video length.
4. Record one part at a time.
5. Ask to expand any part into a full script.
commonFix: If the parts overlap, reply: "Make each part teach something distinct; remove repetition and sharpen the cliffhangers."
promptText:
ROLE: Act as a content strategist who plans connected maths video series.

CONTEXT: A teacher wants a 3-part video series on one chapter for [CLASS/GRADE] students of [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / ICSE / State Board / JEE / NEET]. Each part should stand alone but pull viewers to the next, building from basics to advanced.

YOUR TASK:
1. Take the chapter I give and divide it into 3 distinct parts (Foundations, Core Techniques, Advanced/Exam-level).
2. For each part give: a click-friendly title, the hook, 3 to 5 content beats, one worked example, and a cliffhanger leading to the next part.
3. Ensure no two parts repeat the same teaching.
4. Provide a one-line description and 5 hashtags per part.

INPUT: Here is the chapter, target length per video and level: [PASTE CHAPTER, LENGTH AND CLASS LEVEL HERE].

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: Solve every worked example fully and VERIFY each by two independent methods. Never invent formulas; use standard correct results. Keep all maths legible in plain text or LaTeX. Make sure the difficulty truly increases across parts.

OUTPUT FORMAT (in this order):
SERIES TITLE: one umbrella title.
For each part (Part 1, 2, 3): TITLE | HOOK (spoken) | CONTENT BEATS (bullets) | WORKED EXAMPLE with on-screen maths in [BRACKETS] and final answer | CLIFFHANGER (spoken) | DESCRIPTION + 5 hashtags.
VERIFICATION NOTE: one line per worked example confirming two checks.

RULES: Parts must be distinct and progressively harder. Cliffhangers must be honest about the next part's content. Flawless, legible maths.

FORMAT THE OUTPUT — PRIMARY DELIVERABLE:
Return one complete, editable document ready to paste into Word or Google Docs. Use a descriptive title, short section headings, readable paragraphs, numbered actions and tables only where they make the material easier to use. Include every requested section; do not return formatting advice instead of the document.


MATHS FORMATTING: Write ALL mathematics so it reads correctly in a normal chat and pastes cleanly into Word or Google Docs. Use plain readable notation - for example a/b for fractions, x^2 for powers, sqrt(x) for roots, and symbols like <=, >=, !=, +-, pi, theta, integral and sum. Do NOT output raw LaTeX or code such as \frac{}{}, \sqrt{}, x^{2}, $...$ or \( ... \) - these appear as broken symbols to a teacher in a free chat.
Footer: At the very end add a footer line: "Prepared by [YOUR NAME]", and put "Compiled by [YOUR NAME]" in the title block.

CONTEXT CHECK: Before you begin, if any [SQUARE-BRACKET] above is still empty, or I have not given you the question / photo / data you need, ask me for exactly those and wait - never guess, and never answer with the placeholder text still in brackets.

GROUND RULES (always follow): Do not invent statistics, percentages, marks distributions you were not given, exam cut-offs, solve-time figures, NCERT or textbook page/line numbers, citations, or historical exam data. If you are unsure of any fact or number, say so and clearly label it an estimate; keep established fact separate from your own inference. Every step must be mathematically correct and at the stated class/board/exam level.

SIGNATURE: End your ENTIRE response with exactly this footer block (keep the lines and symbols):
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🔗 Free tools & to reach me: https://yosoyun.github.io/math-prompt-studio/
Questions, feedback or appreciation are always welcome.
